scan_metadata.paper_name: Model-Based Diffusion for Trajectory Optimization (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2407.01573)
scan_metadata.explanation: Static scan of the whole checkout at the pinned commit; no filter. The scanner installed and executed nothing: every statement about runtime behaviour is read from source and is marked as such where it matters. The repository has no tests, no notebooks (.ipynb) and no console entry points; the user interface is the set of scripts named in README.md. 12 candidate source files were evaluated (README.md, setup.py and 10 scripts with a __main__ or module-level run); 11 further files were read as supporting implementation (mbd/__init__.py, mbd/utils.py, mbd/planners/__init__.py, mbd/envs/__init__.py and the seven other environment modules), together with .gitignore, the listing of mbd/assets and the header of mbd/assets/car2d_xref.npy. Three scripts are selected and give four tools owned by cli_wrapper, with six execution assignments. Selection does not establish that execution passes.
evidence_limits: Nothing was executed by the scanner. Runtime statements are read from the repository source and from the installed package sources.

The project environment written by the environment manager during this scan (model-based-diffusion-env; reports/environment-requirements.txt lists brax==0.10.5, mujoco-mjx==3.1.6, jax==0.4.30, tyro==0.8.5) was read, not executed: brax/base.py there contains no `dt`, System derives from mjx.Model (base.py:415), and mujoco/mjx/_src/dataclasses.py:59-63 defines replace as dataclasses.replace, so `env.sys.replace(dt=env.dt)` is expected to raise TypeError in the project environment too.
The same reading was made for brax 0.12.3 with mujoco-mjx 3.3.2 in the local uv cache; both versions agree.

tyro 0.8.5 in the project environment rewrites underscores in flag names to hyphens before parsing (tyro/_cli.py:342-361, read), so the README's underscore spelling such as `--env_name` is expected to be accepted; the first executor should still record the real `--help` output.

`mbd` is installed in editable form: site-packages/__editable__.mbd-0.0.1.pth contains the checkout path, so `mbd.__path__[0]` is expected to be repo/model-based-diffusion/mbd and the results directory repo/model-based-diffusion/results.

tutorials.title: README usage section
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Contract for the commands, not an executable source. Its commands are bound to the scripts above; disagreements with the code are listed in readme_code_disagreements.

tutorials.title: Package metadata
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Setup only. Relevant findings for the environment: `packages=find_packages(include="mdb")` (line 6) misspells the package name, and install_requires (lines 8-24) omits brax, mujoco, flax (imported in mbd/envs/car2d.py:3), etils (mbd/envs/hopper.py:6), scienceplots and manim.

tutorials.title: Visualise the diffusion process
tutorials.description: README.md:60-67. Rolls out every intermediate action trajectory of a saved planner run and writes one stacked Brax HTML page.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Deferred. No argument parsing at all; env_name is hard-coded to humanoidtrack (line 16) and Hsample to 50 (line 19), so the README's `--env_name $ENV_NAME` is ignored. Needs results/humanoidtrack/mu_0ts.npy from a prior full humanoid planner run in the same checkout (lines 21-22). Line 140 uses `env.sys.replace(dt=env.dt)`, which is not accepted by the installed brax 0.10.5 nor by brax 0.12.3 (read, not executed). Reuses results/humanoidtrack/rollouts.pkl if it exists, even when mu_0ts.npy has changed (lines 129-139).

tutorials.title: MBD for black-box optimisation
tutorials.description: README.md:69-76. Six seeds of MBD on the 800-dimensional Rastrigin function; saves the mean best-value curve.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Deferred. No command-line interface: function, dimension, sample count, steps, temperature and seed count are module constants (lines 14-25), so the output is one fixed array and the script cannot be applied to new inputs without editing or re-implementing it. It also saves to results/bbo/ without creating the directory (lines 104-107; `os` is imported but unused), and results/ does not exist in the checkout, so the save is expected to fail on a fresh checkout (read, not executed). Nothing is printed to stdout.

tutorials.title: RL baselines (Brax PPO / SAC)
tutorials.description: README.md:78-85. Trains a PPO or SAC policy with fixed per-environment settings, saves parameters and an HTML rollout.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Deferred. The only argument is env_name (lines 18-20); the training budgets are fixed in the source at 50 to 100 million PPO steps with 2048 to 4096 parallel environments, or 6.5 million SAC steps (lines 31-176), with no flag to reduce them, which is outside the budget of this machine. After training, line 236 uses `env.sys.replace(dt=env.dt)` (same Brax issue). The table has no entry for car2d, humanoidtrack or cartpole and has `pusher`, which get_env does not provide.

tutorials.title: MBD training of an MNIST classifier
tutorials.description: Gradient-free optimisation of a small network on MNIST by MBD. Not mentioned in the README.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Omitted. Undocumented experiment without arguments; downloads MNIST from storage.googleapis.com into the hard-coded /tmp/jax_example_data/ (lines 24, 27-34, 50, 64-70); writes no file and prints no result, accuracy appears only in the tqdm progress text (lines 219-227).

tutorials.title: 1-D reverse SDE illustration
tutorials.description: Percent-format script that draws the paper's illustrative figure (objective, forward densities, reverse trajectories) with NumPy.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Omitted. Didactic figure with no inputs and no saved output: savefig is commented out (line 292) and the script ends in plt.show() (line 293), which shows nothing without a display. Requires scienceplots and the `science` style (lines 17-20), not listed in setup.py. Uses unseeded np.random (lines 196, 219), so it is not reproducible.

tutorials.title: Manim explainer animation
tutorials.description: Presentation animation contrasting model-free and model-based diffusion.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Omitted. Presentation material, not a computation of the method. Requires manim (line 2, not in setup.py) and a LaTeX installation for MathTex (lines 231, 275, 292, 334); launches `manim vis_manim.py -pql ...` through os.system with the preview flag and a path relative to the working directory (lines 426-430); unseeded np.random.

tutorials.title: pushT random-action smoke render
tutorials.description: `main()` (lines 77-98) steps the pushT environment with random actions and writes results/pushT/vis.html.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Omitted (internal). Undocumented developer check of an environment, not a user task; line 89 uses `env.sys.replace(dt=env.dt)` (same Brax issue). The PushT class itself is supporting implementation for the planner tools.

cross_cutting_findings: Output location: every writing script uses `<mbd package dir>/../results/...` (mbd_planner.py:153, mbd_opt.py:105, vis_diffusion.py:21, train_brax.py:194, pushT.py:90). With the package imported from the checkout this is repo/model-based-diffusion/results/, which does not exist at the pinned commit and is ignored by .gitignore line 176. No script takes an output-directory argument. Runs for the same environment overwrite each other, so executors and the wrapper must run one command at a time and copy artefacts out immediately.

The four selected commands parse arguments with tyro.cli (mbd_planner.py:186, path_integral.py:152, run_mbd.py:68). vis_diffusion.py, mbd_opt.py and mbd_mnist.py do not read sys.argv at all: passing `--help` to them would start the full computation.

Importing `mbd` imports jax, brax, matplotlib and both planner modules (mbd/__init__.py:1, mbd/planners/__init__.py, mbd/utils.py:1-2, mbd/envs/__init__.py:1-10), so every command is a heavy job even for car2d. mbd_planner.py imports matplotlib.pyplot at line 9; set MPLBACKEND=Agg on this machine without a display.

Brax API split inside the repository: mbd_planner.py:174 uses `sys.tree_replace({"opt.timestep": ...})` (changed in upstream commit c4508b6, 2024-06-12), while path_integral.py:101, vis_diffusion.py:140, train_brax.py:236, pushT.py:89 and cartpole.py:18 still use `sys.replace(dt=...)`. In the installed brax 0.10.5, `brax/base.py` has no `dt` and `brax/envs/base.py:133-135` computes dt from `sys.opt.timestep`; `tree_replace` exists at base.py:114.

Determinism: all selected commands draw randomness only from jax.random.PRNGKey(seed) (mbd_planner.py:40, path_integral.py:57). Car2d.reset ignores the key (car2d.py:73-75), so the seed changes only the sampling noise there. Results should be compared on the same device and package versions; the run-time line of run_mbd.py is not reproducible.

Default sizes that matter on an 8 GB GPU: 2048 samples x 50 steps x 99 reverse steps for most environments; humanoidrun is raised to 8192 samples and 300 steps and pushT to 200 steps unless --disable_recommended_params is given (mbd_planner.py:54-68). Only car2d and hopper are proposed for execution; other environments remain documented but unexecuted unless the coordinator adds assignments.
open_questions: Does path_integral_hopper_mppi really fail at path_integral.py:100-102 with the installed brax 0.10.5, as the source reading predicts? The answer decides whether mbd_run_baseline_planner and the path_integral option of the two run_mbd tools exist. An older Brax that still has `System.dt` would be a different environment decision and is not proposed here.
Should the black-box benchmark be promoted to a parameterless reproduction tool (it is a README headline use but returns one fixed array and needs results/bbo created first)? Deferred by default.

Should further environments (ant, halfcheetah, walker2d, pushT, humanoidstandup, humanoidrun, humanoidtrack) be executed before the planner tool advertises them, or should the tool accept them as documented-but-unverified with that stated in USAGE.md?
Feasible sample count for the Brax hopper run on the 8 GB GPU is not known to the scanner; the fallback through --Nsample is described in the execution assignment.
